reason: E1 shows that thermal exposure at 800°C forms a protective chromium-oxide layer and a spinel coating on a similar HEA, and states these layers enhance wear resistance, directly supporting the first three premises. However, E1 does not address pre-oxidation as a controlled treatment before sliding, and E2 concerns a different alloy and lower temperature, providing no support for the specific coating or conditions. The cited evidence thus supports the oxide formation and protective role but leaves the pre-oxidation intervention premise without direct prior evidence.
premises: Thermal exposure at 800°C forms a protective Cr2O3-rich oxide layer on FeNiCrCoCu HEA
This oxide layer acts as a barrier reducing direct metal contact and microcrack propagation
The oxide layer reduces wear and microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding
Pre-oxidation treatment can produce a continuous, adherent oxide film prior to wear testing
